explanation: The top of a lighthouse is its lantern, and the one who tends it is the keeper. The film's watchman and his grey cat won the Gold Gull a year after its release.

claims.text: Only the answer fits clues 1 to 3.
Its hero tends a light on a sea rock for thirty winters, with a grey cat for company.
It won the fixture Gold Gull prize in 1988, the year after it came out.
Its title names the job of whoever tends the lamp at the top of a lighthouse.
One word of its title names the glass room that holds a lighthouse's lamp.
Each distractor contradicts at least one of clues 1 to 3.

writerNotes: Invented fixture for tests, the mock backend and the e2e track (ARCHITECTURE 5.6). Not a real fact; never scheduled on the main track. Every film in the list is invented, so the ladder is solved from the titles and years the suggestions show (R1-30). RITE round 3 (R3-04) found clue 1 typed into one match: it named the job, and "keeper" listed this film alone. Now clue 1 is the story, which no title word repeats: "light" or "lighthouse" lists four Lighthouse films and never this one, and "keeper" lists four Keeper films, so a clue-1 solve takes the step from a lighthouse to its lantern. Clue 2's year keeps only the 1987 film, clue 3 is the job, and the three other Keepers on clue 4 fit clue 3, each ruled out by its year. Clue 4, the lantern, is a fact of its own.
